10.0.0.en: "Ask ye of the LORD rain in the time of the latter rain; so the LORD shall make lightnings, and give them showers of rain, to every one grass in the field" [1].

10.0.1.en: In ancient times, because of evil, Elijah stopped the rain for three years and six months so that all might be disciplined and the rain come down, and so our sins hold back the overflow of God's abundant graces upon us and deprive us of His rain that turns the barren wilderness into a garden that gladdens His heart (Song 5:1).

10.0.2.en: In our study of the Book of Hosea (6:3) we noticed that in Palestine an early rain falls where the seed is sown, and a latter rain by which the crop is ripened; the first rain signifies the work of the Holy Spirit through the Law and the prophecies, etc., before the coming of the Lord, while the latter signifies the abundance of the descent of the Holy Spirit upon the Church of the New Covenant, which Joel the prophet announced: "I will pour out my spirit upon all flesh" (Joel 2:28).

10.0.3.en: We can say that the early rain is the Law and the prophecies that the Lord gave to the men of the Old Testament, while the latter rain is the preaching of the Gospel, which uncovers the mysteries of God and gives us deep knowledge and a vision of the divine life.

10.0.4.en: St. Didymus the Blind sees that the early rain also means the teachings concerning the Incarnation of the Savior, while the latter rain is the enjoyment of the mysteries of His divinity.

10.0.5.en: In any case, let us not cease to ask God without interruption that He may flash in our hearts with the splendor of His glory, giving us His latter rain to water our land with His divine love and give it multiplied fruit.

10.1.0.en: 2 For the teraphim have spoken vanity, and the diviners have seen a lie, and have told false dreams; they comfort in vain: therefore they went their way as a flock, they were humbled, because there was no shepherd. 3 "Mine anger was kindled against the shepherds, and I punished the he-goats: for the LORD of hosts hath visited his flock the house of Judah, and hath made them as his goodly horse in the battle.

10.1.1.en: Though God sends rain on the righteous and the wicked, He does not give the spiritual rain except to those who ask for it; and now, for Him to take care of His flock spiritually, this flock must abandon the deceptions of divination and sorcery and the dreams of the false prophets so that He Himself may shepherd His people.

10.1.2.en: "For the teraphim have spoken vanity, and the diviners have seen a lie, and have told false dreams; they deceive with vanity, therefore they went their way as a flock. They were humbled because there is no shepherd. Mine anger was kindled against the shepherds, and I punished the he-goats: for the LORD of hosts hath visited his flock the house of Judah, and hath made them as his goodly horse in the battle" [2-3].

10.1.3.en: The teraphim are statues of gods that they set up inside the houses as guardians for them and to consult before every action. God cannot take over the care of His people as long as they rely on the teraphim and ask divination and resort to the dreams of the false prophets, for all these may placate a man and deceive him with soft, deceptive words, but those who rely on them do not fall into humiliation, since they are without care. And now, as the people leave these vain deceptions, the Lord does two works: He declares His wrath against the corrupt shepherds and takes over the shepherding Himself, as He affirmed in the Book of Ezekiel: "Behold, I will inquire after my sheep and visit them... I will feed my flock, and I will cause them to lie down, saith the Lord GOD" (Ezek 34:11, 15). He punishes the evil he-goats (the rams) and takes care of His flock, giving His life as a ransom for it (Jn 10:11). He gives them His life that is able to set them up as a horse in the procession of salvation, able to fight against the devil and his works. And as it was said: "Was the LORD displeased against the rivers? was thine anger against the rivers? was thy wrath against the sea, that thou didst ride upon thine horses and thy chariots of salvation?" (Hab 3:8).

10.2.s.en: 3. Enjoying victory and the restoration of the kingdom:

10.2.0.en: 4 Out of him is the corner, out of him the nail, out of him the battle bow, out of him shall come forth every oppressor together. 5 And they shall be as mighty men, treading the mire of the streets in the battle: and they shall fight, because the LORD is with them, and the riders on horses shall be confounded. 6 And I will strengthen the house of Judah, and I will save the house of Joseph, and I will bring them again; for I have mercy upon them: and they shall be as though I had not cast them off: for I am the LORD their God, and will hear them. 7 And they of Ephraim shall be like a mighty man, and their heart shall rejoice as through wine: yea, their children shall see it, and be glad; their heart shall rejoice in the LORD. 8 I will whistle for them, and gather them; for I have redeemed them: and they shall increase as they have increased. 9 And I will sow them among the people: and they shall remember me in far countries; and they shall live with their children, and turn again. 10 I will bring them again also out of the land of Egypt, and gather them out of Assyria; and I will bring them into the land of Gilead and Lebanon; and place shall not be found for them. 11 And he shall pass through the sea of affliction, and shall smite the depths in the sea, and all the deeps of the river shall dry up: and the pride of Assyria shall be brought down, and the sceptre of Egypt shall depart away. 12 And I will strengthen them in the LORD; and they shall walk in his name, saith the LORD.

10.2.1.en: The fruit of God's personal care is their enjoyment of victory and security and joy and the restoration of God's kingdom among them.

10.2.2.en: First: "Out of him is the corner, out of him the nail, out of him the battle bow, out of him shall come forth every oppressor speedily" [4]. True divine care appears in the manifestation of the Lord Christ among His people as a cornerstone that binds all together in Him and supports all with one spirit. He also appears among them as a nail (peg) that supports their temporal tent, that is, their temporary life, so that the winds of strange teachings do not move it nor the storms of the love of the world and the lusts of the flesh. This is the divine peg that supports the body (the tent) by its sanctification for the sake of the Kingdom of God. And the Lord is also among them a battle bow that the believer aims, fighting evil and sin, so that it is said of them: "One of you shall chase a thousand, and two put ten thousand to flight" (Deut 32:30), and they, as soldiers of the Lord carrying the Lord Christ as their true arrow, say: "For we wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against principalities, against powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this world, against spiritual wickedness in high places" (Eph 6:13).

10.2.3.en: As for His saying: "out of him shall come forth every oppressor speedily," it refers to His work in His Church, which receives Him as cornerstone and nail and spiritual bow, as He removes from it the oppressor and the corrupter so that all in it may be sanctified by Him.

10.3.0.en: Second: "And they shall be as mighty men, treading the mire of the streets in the battle: and they shall fight, because the LORD is with them, and the riders on horses shall be confounded" [5]. This is their might and this is their victory, that they tread the mire of the streets; so he is not like him who had the talent and buried it in the earth (Mt 25:18), but by the heavenly Lord they rise above every material thought, soaring in the heavenly places, however violent this thought may seem, like riders of horses.

10.3.1.en: St. Didymus the Blind distinguishes between riders of horses and horsemen; the riders of horses are those who mount them without controlling them with a bridle, for if horses signify the body, the soul mounts the body and leaves it in its unruliness and stubbornness, so this soul is put to shame because of the lusts of the body. The horses also signify arrogant sophistical thoughts which the soul mounts and so falls into pride and is deprived of salvation. Of the riders of horses it was said: "the horse and his rider hath he thrown into the sea" (Ex 15:1), "Some trust in chariots, and some in horses: but we will remember the name of the LORD our God" (Ps 20:7), "An horse is a vain thing for safety" (Ps 33:7). This is concerning the riders of horses, while the horsemen signify him who mounts the horse or steed controlling it with a bridle, for it was said to Elijah the prophet: "My father, my father, the chariot of Israel, and the horsemen thereof" (2 Kgs 2:12).

10.4.0.en: Third: He compensates them for the years that the locust has eaten, so in place of the losses that befell them on the day the Lord rejected them they receive great blessings that cover the former losses, for He says: "And I will strengthen the house of Judah, and I will save the house of Joseph, and I will bring them again; for I have mercy upon them: and they shall be as though I had not cast them off: for I am the LORD their God, and will hear them" [6]. Why does He speak of the house of Judah and the house of Joseph? Because from the first house came forth Jesus, the giver of salvation, and from the second house appeared Joseph, a type of Christ, who provided wheat after hunger and famine had crushed them (Gen 41:56). If Israel passed through years of famine, the true Joseph satisfies them, as St. Mary says: "He hath filled the hungry with good things" (Lk 1:53). He is the Lord their God who answers their request and satisfies their needs, so they no longer remember the past with its harsh spiritual famine, for the joys of the present cover all the sorrows of the past. Therefore He says: "And they of Ephraim shall be like a mighty man, and their heart shall rejoice as through wine" [7]. This is the mark of the messianic age: the joy of the Holy Spirit, which the world cannot take away from the heart!

10.4.1.en: Here he mentions Ephraim as a mighty man filled with joy, perhaps an allusion to the northern kingdom, which lived in captivity for a longer time than Judah, so He affirmed His support for it. Perhaps he meant the tribe of Ephraim in particular, because it was the violent one that was the first instigator of the corruption of the northern kingdom, especially as Jeroboam, who incited the ten tribes to rebel against Judah, was an Ephraimite (1 Kgs 11:26; 12:2), and it was he who established idol worship in Israel (1 Kgs 12:25-33). Now the Lord assures Ephraim that he becomes spiritually like a mighty man and his heart is filled with joy.

10.5.0.en: Fourth: He gathers their dispersion and makes them grow in His bosom: "I will whistle for them, and gather them; for I have redeemed them: and they shall increase as they have increased" [8]. He is like the beekeeper who whistles to his scattered bees to gather honey from the meadows and gardens. He gathers them to Himself and grants them by blessing to grow and multiply as they had formerly multiplied, meaning that if He cared for them while they were under chastening, under the bondage of Pharaoh, so that they grew as much as they humbled them (Ex 1:7), will He not rather make them grow and multiply when He redeems them from bondage?!

10.5.1.en: He fulfills in them His promise to Abraham, the father of the fathers: "for I will make thee a father of a multitude of nations. And I will make thee exceeding fruitful, and I will make nations of thee" (Gen 17:5-6), and as it was said in Isaiah: "A little one shall become a thousand, and a small one a strong nation" (Isa 60:22). And as St. Didymus the Blind says: [If these words were taken literally they would appear difficult, for many of the saints had no children at all, like Elijah and Elisha and John the Baptist, to whom no one attained in virtue and in the knowledge of the holy mysteries (Mt 11:11), and yet he had no children; therefore we must understand that spiritually]. So from one side they have children in the Spirit, like those whom Paul begot in the Gospel (1 Cor 4:15), for whom he travailed until Christ be formed in them (Gal 4:19), or those whom Peter the Apostle calls "obedient children" (1 Pet 1:14), and from another side they have children in the heart, that is, the fruits of the Holy Spirit manifested in us as children who rejoice God's heart!

10.6.0.en: Fifth: As He brings them back to Himself to grow and bear fruit by the Holy Spirit, He again sows them among the peoples as living seed buried in the earth to bring forth much fruit, for He says: "And I will sow them among the people: and they shall remember me in far countries; and they shall live with their children, and turn again. And I will bring them again also out of the land of Egypt, and gather them out of Assyria; and I will bring them into the land of Gilead and Lebanon; and place shall not be found for them. And he shall pass through the sea of affliction, and shall smite the depths in the sea, and all the deeps of the river shall dry up: and the pride of Assyria shall be brought down, and the sceptre of Egypt shall depart away. And I will strengthen them in the LORD; and they shall walk in his name, saith the LORD" [9-12].

10.6.1.en: What a living and joyful picture of God's work in them: after He gathers them from the captivity of sin and brings them back to Himself, He casts them as living seed among the peoples to witness to salvation in far lands and to have spiritual sons in the Lord. But they do not walk in the spirit of the world; rather their hearts return from the symbolic land of Egypt, that is, the love of the world, and the Lord gathers them from Assyria, that is, from the spirit of pride, and brings them to the land of Gilead and Lebanon; and lest this be understood materially He said: "and place shall not be found for them," for they are in a state of continual migration and constant going forth from strength to strength and from glory to glory, their hearts raised in the heavenly places, with no place on earth!

10.6.2.en: St. Didymus the Blind comments on this statement as a declaration of the spiritual migration of the believer: [who passes from vice to virtue. This is truly a change of country, a change from sin to righteousness, from evil to godliness... and he goes from virtue to virtue (Ps 83:8), and passes from the shadow of the Law, where is the letter that kills, to reach the Spirit that gives life (2 Cor 3:6)]... St. Didymus also sees that the migration to the spiritual Lebanon is a migration to the state of deification, that is, the enjoyment of the attributes of the Lord Jesus, where the soul enters into the glorious holy Church, "not having spot, or wrinkle, or any such thing" (Eph 5:27), of which it is said: "the smell of thy garments is like the smell of Lebanon" (Song 4:11).

10.7.0.en: As He brings them into the new Lebanon, that is, the holy life of the Church, He passes with them through the sea of affliction, like the living fish that hides in the waters with all their disturbances and the sea with all its waves without losing its life... They enter into affliction in this world but the depths of the world cannot swallow them nor the deeps of the river draw them away! Rather they come out of every affliction with greater strength, declaring the Kingdom of God within them; therefore He ends His speech about the blessings of this age by saying: "And I will strengthen them in the LORD; and they shall walk in his name, saith the LORD" [12].

11.0.s.en: 1. A lament over those who reject:

11.0.0.en: 1 Open thy doors, O Lebanon, that the fire may devour thy cedars. 2 Howl, O cypress; for the cedar is fallen; because the mighty are ruined: howl, O ye oaks of Bashan; for the impenetrable forest is come down. 3 There is a voice of the howling of the shepherds; for their glory is ruined: a voice of the roaring of young lions; for the pride of Jordan is ruined.

11.0.1.en: Israel's rejection of the Lord Christ turned it into total ruin, so the prophet laments it, saying: "Open thy doors, O Lebanon, that the fire may devour thy cedars. Howl, O cypress; for the cedar is fallen; because the mighty are struck: howl, O ye oaks of Bashan; for the impenetrable forest is come down. There is a voice of the howling of the shepherds; for their glory is ruined: a voice of the roaring of young lions; for the pride of Jordan is ruined" [1-3].

11.0.2.en: And it is noticed in this lament:

11.0.3.en: First: that the ruin carries extended and comprehensive dimensions, striking Lebanon and Bashan and the Jordan, as if the Jews' rejection of the Lord Christ brought them down under an extended, almost collective blow, for they cried out, "His blood be on us, and on our children." And the comprehensiveness does not stop at places but includes the kinds of trees: the cedar that is burned with fire and the cypress that howls and also the oak, as the trees of the forest fall, etc...

11.0.4.en: Second: He calls nature to mourn for the man who denied his Creator and rejected His work of salvation and even betrayed Him for thirty pieces of silver.

11.0.5.en: Third: What he mentions here was fulfilled literally, for it was the custom of enemies, when they seized a fertile land like the Promised Land, to cut down its trees to profit from their wood or to burn them with fire with the intent of destruction and ruin.

11.0.6.en: Fourth: From the symbolic side, what does Lebanon signify in his saying: "Open thy doors, O Lebanon, that the fire may devour thy cedars"? The enemies entered Lebanon through its doors, that is, through the entrances of the mountains that lead to the city, in order to destroy its cedars of which it is proud. We saw Lebanon spiritually in the previous chapter as signifying the migration to the holy Church to bear in us the sweet fragrance of Christ, for it is said: "the smell of thy garments is like the smell of Lebanon" (Song 4:11). And as Lebanon signifies the fruitful Church that bears the attributes of the Lord and His fragrance and the fruit of His Holy Spirit, it also, as St. Didymus the Blind says, signifies on the other side paganism (apostasy from the faith) and arrogance, for he says: [Indeed when the Bridegroom in the Song of Songs calls the Church of the victorious He says to her: Come with me from Lebanon, my spouse (Song 4:8)... she comes to Him who calls her from ignorance and unbelief to holy knowledge and perfect faith].

11.0.7.en: Fifth: What befalls the cedar and the cypress and the oak and the forest signifies the Jewish groups that rejected the Messiah the Savior, and also signifies the sins that lie hidden in the soul which drive man to be deprived of enjoying salvation. St. Didymus the Blind sees in the haughty cedar an allusion to the company of the proud or to the demon of pride, for he says: [It is written in Isaiah against these barren, fruitless trees: "For the day of the LORD of hosts shall be upon every one that is proud and lofty, and upon every one that is lifted up; and he shall be brought low" (Isa 2:12), and a little after: "And upon all the cedars of Lebanon, that are high and lifted up, and upon all the oaks of Bashan" (Zech 2:13). These wild trees grow upon pride... They will be consumed by the fire, the corrupt, the diligent, as Isaiah himself says: "and Lebanon shall fall by a mighty one" (Isa 10:34)]. St. Didymus also sees that if the cedar signifies the pride of the great, then the cypress, which is a small tree, signifies those subject to them; if the cedar signifies those who are wise and prudent in their own eyes, then the cypress signifies those who walk in their current. Therefore when fire devours the cedar the cypress mourns the fall of the mighty who are their lords in their eyes.

11.0.8.en: As for the oak of Bashan, it signifies the dense forests full of leafy trees but without fruit; they represent the hypocrites who have the appearance of religion and deny its power. And the forest is the trees found in the wildernesses and also without fruit!

11.0.9.en: Sixth: The prophet turned in his speech to the shepherds who left their pastoral work and began to howl because the young lions roar to devour and there is none to deliver, and because the Jordan with its pride, because of the dense forests and the trees in which the wild beasts hide, has been ruined.

11.0.10.en: This is the broad outline of the lament that the prophet laid upon every soul that rejects the work of salvation in it: its doors open before the enemy so that it loses all its trees, nature grieves over it, and eternal spiritual destruction comes upon it.

11.1.0.en: 4 Thus saith the LORD my God; "Feed the flock of the slaughter; 5 Whose possessors slay them, and hold themselves not guilty: and they that sell them say, Blessed be the LORD; for I am rich: and their own shepherds pity them not. 6 For I will no more pity the inhabitants of the land, saith the LORD: but, lo, I will deliver the men every one into his neighbour's hand, and into the hand of his king: and they shall smite the land, and out of their hand I will not deliver them."

11.1.1.en: "Thus saith the LORD my God; Feed the flock of the slaughter, whose possessors slay them, and hold themselves not guilty: and they that sell them say, Blessed be the LORD; for I am rich: and their own shepherds pity them not" [4-5].

11.1.2.en: Since they rejected the Messiah, the sacrificial Lamb, for their own sake, for perdition and destruction, they became, by their rejection of salvation, without price; their owners slay them and it is not counted against them as sin since they deserve slaughter; and if their owner sells them he is relieved of them as they were a burden to him, so at the sale he says: Blessed be the LORD, I am rich. Perhaps by this he portrays for us the condition of the Jews after they rejected the Savior, as they were scattered in many lands and were exposed to bitter persecutions, every nation wishing to be rid of them as a burden upon them.

11.1.3.en: The wonder is that God allows the wicked to have harsh shepherds in order to discipline them, for He says: "their own shepherds pity them not." For shepherds are from God; when He is pleased with His people He says: "And I will give you pastors according to mine heart, which shall feed you with knowledge and understanding" (Jer 3:15), that is, they offer them pastures of knowledge and understanding or pastures of divine wisdom that come from God (Eph 4:11; 1 Cor 12:28); but when He is angry with His people He leaves them to themselves and they feed in the pastures of "the wisdom of this world" (1 Cor 2:6), and He delivers them to the pasture of "a reprobate mind" (Rom 1:28), and the pasture of "vile affections" (Rom 1:26).

11.1.4.en: Good shepherds lead the flock into the bosom of God so that they enjoy security, but the wicked drive them outside God so that they perish; therefore the Psalmist says: "For, lo, they that are far from thee shall perish: thou destroyest all them that go a whoring from thee. But it is good for me to draw near to God: I have made the Lord GOD my refuge, that I may declare all thy works" (Ps 73:27).

11.2.0.en: They rejected the Good Shepherd, the Messiah the Savior, so they were deprived even of good shepherds, and the Lord delivered them to shepherds who have no pity on the flock... since He Himself no longer has pity on them, for He says: "For I will no more pity the inhabitants of the land, saith the LORD: but, lo, I will deliver the men every one into his neighbour's hand, and into the hand of his king: and they shall smite the land, and out of their hand I will not deliver them" [6]. He called them "the inhabitants of the land" because they rejected the heavenly Messiah, who came to raise them from earth to heaven, so they remained in their hearts on the earth and were counted "inhabitants of the land" and even bore in them the nature of the earth. This earthly nature bears neither heavenly love nor largeness of heart, but every man delivers his brother to affliction and injustice for his destruction.

11.3.0.en: 7 And I fed the flock of slaughter; but they are the most downtrodden of the flock. And I took unto me two staves; the one I called Grace, and the other I called Bands; and I fed the flock. 8 Three shepherds also I cut off in one month; and my soul was distressed with them, and their soul also hated me. 9 Then said I, I will not feed you: that that dieth, let it die; and that that is to be cut off, let it be cut off; and let the rest eat every one the flesh of another. 10 And I took my staff, even Grace, and cut it asunder, that I might break my covenant which I had made with all the tribes. 11 And it was broken in that day: and so the most downtrodden of the flock that waited upon me knew that it was the word of the LORD.

11.3.1.en: It was the custom in ancient times for the shepherd to hold two staves, with one of which he struck any wild beast that attacked the flock and with the other he led the flock so that it would not stray from the way, but the Lord appears here holding two staves, which are: grace or beauty, and bands or union; so He leads us by His grace in His green heavenly pastures that we may lack nothing, and leads us by union to bind us all together in Him by the spirit of divine love.

11.3.2.en: St. Didymus the Blind sees that God by these two staves leads the Jews as He leads the Gentiles as His rational flock, and the two staves also signify His work as Savior and as King.

11.4.0.en: In any case, by the Jews' rejection of the Messiah the King, the Lord broke the staff of Grace, so they were deprived of divine help and lost His blessings because they broke His covenant. Thus they lost His compassionate care: "Then said I, I will not feed you: that that dieth, let it die; and that that is to be cut off, let it be cut off; and let the rest eat every one the flesh of another" [9], not out of contempt for the sheep but because of His sanctification of human freedom, so He left them to themselves, by themselves, apart from His grace.

11.4.1.en: He says: "Three shepherds also I cut off in one month; and my soul was distressed with them, and their soul also hated me" [8]. Who are these three shepherds whom the Lord destroyed and whom the Jews lost? St. Jerome sees that these three are Moses, Aaron and Miriam, who died shortly before the people entered the Promised Land. Perhaps he means that by their rejection of the Lord Christ they lost His threefold care as priest and king and giver of prophecy, so they were deprived of His atoning intercession (His priesthood) and of His kingship as a leader who conquers and brings them into victory, and of the giver of prophecy who reveals to them the mysteries of the life to come. In ancient times the king was not the priest and not the seer or prophet, but in Christ these three were gathered on a surpassing and unique level.

11.5.0.en: 12 And I said unto them, If ye think good, give me my wages; and if not, forbear. So they weighed for my wages thirty pieces of silver. 13 And the LORD said unto me, Cast it unto the potter: a goodly price that I was prised at of them. And I took the thirty pieces of silver, and cast them to the potter in the house of the LORD. 14 Then I cut asunder mine other staff, even Bands, that I might break the brotherhood between Judah and Israel.

11.5.1.en: God did not want to present this dark picture of what the people of the circumcision came to because of their rejection of the Messiah without revealing the picture of this rejection in the act of betrayal that Judas committed against his Lord for thirty pieces of silver, which represents the betrayal of the whole people, for they valued Him at the price of a slave who deserves death.

11.5.2.en: "And I said unto them, If ye think good, give me my wages; and if not, forbear. So they weighed for my wages thirty pieces of silver. And the LORD said unto me, Cast it unto the potter in the house of the LORD" [12-13].

11.5.3.en: First: What is the silver that was offered as the price of betraying the Lord? St. Didymus the Blind says: [Let us take the wages and the silver from the spiritual side. Silver often signifies divine knowledge and the divine word, as in the saying: "The words of the LORD are pure words: as silver tried in a furnace of earth, purified seven times" (Ps 12:6), and it is said in Proverbs: "The tongue of the just is as choice silver" (Prov 10:2). Here the word "tongue" means "speech." But not every word of "silver" is taken in a good sense, for the Lord says of the erring priests of the Jews: "Thy silver is become dross" (Isa 1:22). Here He does not accuse the silver in itself but their deceptive speech, so the Lord says of those who utter this speech: "Reprobate silver shall men call them, because the LORD hath rejected them" (Jer 6:3), since He rejected the deceivers of zeal and the breakers of the commandments. In the same way we understand what is said in Proverbs that silver given to deceit must be taken as a piece of pottery (Prov 26:23); this is the speech of those who care only for earthly things (earthen pottery), of whom it was said by Isaiah: "their voice comes from the earth" (Isa 8:19). So there are kinds of silver, for since the people of the circumcision decided on a wage for Him who suffered for them of thirty pieces of silver (Mt 20:28; Mk 10:5; Jn 10:15)... they paid adulterated silver... presenting deceitful words. And in Christianity also there are people whose beliefs are wrong, "those who walk in craftiness and adulterate the word of God" (2 Cor 4:2), understanding the word of God according to their passions. Of these we must beware and count their talk adulterated silver].

11.5.4.en: It is as though the Jews and the heretics, as they present adulterated and deceitful words, sell the Lord for adulterated silver!

11.5.5.en: Second: They counted Him a slave, so they paid the price, thirty pieces of silver, the price of a slave (Ex 21:32). Perhaps the number 30 symbolizes the defilement of the five senses, for if the number 6 signifies deficiency, then the number 5 (the senses) multiplied by 6 yields 30. It is as though the price of betraying the Lord Christ is the defilement of our senses for the benefit of His enemy the devil instead of sanctifying them to Him.

11.5.6.en: Third: What does he mean by the potter into whose house the silver was cast in the house of the Lord? St. Didymus the Blind sees that the adulterated silver that was paid as a price for the Lord Christ for betraying Him meets in the house of Holy Scripture, which is the house of the potter, where is the testing fire, which exposes their deceptions and reveals their contradiction with the prophecies concerning the Lord.

11.5.7.en: Fourth: As the potter deals with dust and clay with fire, the casting of silver into the potter's house declares the nature of their earthly, dusty heart; it is not fitting that it be put in palaces or treasuries but in the dust.

11.5.8.en: Fifth: With this price a field was bought, called "the field of blood," used for the burial of strangers (Mt 27:7), an allusion to the acceptance of the Gentiles, where we are buried with Christ by the price of His blood that we may rise with Him. St. Jerome says: [The price of Christ is the place of our burial, and the field has been called "the field of blood"; it is the field of the blood of the Jews but it is the place of our burial, because we are strangers and foreigners and have no place of rest. He was crucified and died and we were buried with Him].

11.6.0.en: Sixth: He ends His speech about the rejection of the Messiah and their betrayal of Him by saying: "Then I cut asunder mine other staff, even Bands (union), that I might break the brotherhood between Judah and Israel" [14]. St. Didymus the Blind sees that the two staves will come together and be united as one staff, as it is written in (Ezek 37), when the Jews return at the end of the ages and accept the Lord Christ, and so become with Judah (the Church of the New Covenant) one by entering the faith.

11.7.0.en: 15 And the LORD said unto me, Take unto thee yet the instruments of a foolish shepherd. 16 For, lo, I will raise up a shepherd in the land, which shall not visit those that be cut off, neither shall seek that which is driven away, nor heal that which is broken, nor feed that which standeth still: but he shall eat the flesh of the fat, and tear their hoofs in pieces. 17 Woe to the worthless shepherd that leaveth the flock! the sword shall be upon his arm, and upon his right eye: his arm shall be clean dried up, and his right eye shall be utterly darkened.

11.8.0.en: Since they rejected the Lord Christ, the Good Shepherd, they were deprived of divine grace and of unity together in the Lord by the breaking of the two staves and accepted the false shepherding of the Antichrist, for He says: "Take unto thee yet the instruments of a foolish shepherd, for, lo, I will raise up a shepherd in the land, which shall not visit those that be cut off, neither shall seek that which is driven away, nor heal that which is broken, nor feed that which standeth still: but he shall eat the flesh of the fat, and tear their hoofs in pieces" [16].

11.8.1.en: St. Didymus the Blind comments on this statement, saying: [God, who leaves them in their shame, has raised up for them a foolish shepherd without experience in shepherding, who destroys those who chose him as their shepherd. He does not care for the one who strayed and became alone, far from the flock, to bring him back, who separated by his straying. He does not preserve anything, nor seek those who were scattered, nor care for the wounded, nor lead the healthy. His aim is evil and not good; he runs after his own advantage and his greed, so he devours the flesh and tears off the hoofs of those under his care. He is not like the shepherds whom God gives, saying: "And I will give you pastors according to mine heart, which shall feed you with knowledge and understanding" (Jer 3:15). For can they be anything but good shepherds, those whose head is He who gives His life for the sheep as the Good Shepherd (Jn 10:15)...? For it was said: "And when the chief Shepherd shall appear, ye shall receive a crown of glory that fadeth not away" (1 Pet 5:4). Those who shepherd the sheep thus do not lord it over those who are their charge (1 Pet 5:3), while those who eat the flesh of the sheep seek their own pleasure, thinking that they find glory in the shame of their deeds. They eat without discrimination, so their god is their belly (Phil 3:19) and they are slaves to it, not slaves of Christ Jesus. Of these the Apostle writes: "For they that are such serve not our Lord Jesus Christ, but their own belly" (Rom 16:18)].

11.8.2.en: What does he mean by tearing off the nails? Good shepherds keep "the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace" (Eph 4:3), but the wicked tear from the flock its nails, as they are torn from the fingers, that is, they cause it to lose its unity.

11.9.0.en: This is the fruit of the people's evil: the Lord leaves it to a foolish shepherd who scatters it as he scatters himself, for He says: "Woe to the worthless shepherd that leaveth the flock! the sword shall be upon his arm, and upon his right eye: his arm shall be clean dried up, and his right eye shall be utterly darkened" [17]. And as St. Didymus the Blind says concerning this sword which shatters the arm of the foolish shepherd and his right eye: [The word of God threatens especially the bad shepherds... So the Lord says in Isaiah: "If ye be willing and obedient, ye shall eat the good of the land: but if ye refuse and rebel, ye shall be devoured with the sword" (Isa 1:19-20), and He speaks in Jeremiah of the avenging sword: "I will stretch out my hand upon the inhabitants of the land" (Jer 6:12) so that they perish... The avenging sword is upon the arm (of the foolish shepherd) and his eye, that is, it touches the two senses of work and contemplation, so his arm is dried up as it becomes a dead member, and his right eye is struck with blindness...].

11.9.1.en: St. Didymus sees in this prophecy a reference to the Antichrist, who has a strong arm through the signs he performs (2 Thess 2:9), while his right eye signifies his intellectual deceptions, as he claims perfect knowledge though he is a liar (1 Tim 6:20), and Elymas the sorcerer bore a symbol of him, who deceived by his sorcerous works and his lies, so his works were nullified and he was struck with blindness so that he did not see the sun (Acts 13:10).
